yves-salomon.origin: Yves Salomon is a French house associated with fur, shearling and luxury outerwear, not a fiber class. User shorthand Yves Solomon maps to producer spelling Salomon. Fiber or fur still comes from animal sources specified per product rather than from the house name. This atlas treats the trademark as educational vocabulary for reading hangtags, mill cloth names and generic fiber classes without certifying supply chains, performance claims or animal welfare.
yves-salomon.structure: The house name does not define a single keratin chemistry. Products may use fur, shearling, wool or cashmere cloths depending on the SKU, so learners should read construction and fiber content instead of inferring a house-wide material. This atlas treats the trademark as educational vocabulary for reading hangtags, mill cloth names and generic fiber classes without certifying supply chains, performance claims or animal welfare.
yves-salomon.process: Furrier and outerwear making traditions sit beside woven and knitted cloth garments. Cutting, sewing and finishing routes differ for shearling coats versus cashmere wraps, which is why composition must be checked on each ticket. This atlas treats the trademark as educational vocabulary for reading hangtags, mill cloth names and generic fiber classes without certifying supply chains, performance claims or animal welfare.
yves-salomon.performance: Warmth, hand and durability follow the actual material, for example shearling versus cashmere coating, not the house name alone. Treat marketing adjectives as cues to verify rather than as lab results. This atlas treats the trademark as educational vocabulary for reading hangtags, mill cloth names and generic fiber classes without certifying supply chains, performance claims or animal welfare.
yves-salomon.identify: No test identifies Yves Salomon as a fiber. Identify fur, shearling, wool or cashmere by labeling and, where needed, standard textile methods for fiber type and diameter. This atlas treats the trademark as educational vocabulary for reading hangtags, mill cloth names and generic fiber classes without certifying supply chains, performance claims or animal welfare.
yves-salomon.labeling: Fur and textile labeling rules differ by jurisdiction. Generic fiber or fur names still matter beside the house trademark, and this atlas does not reinterpret national fur labeling schemes. This atlas treats the trademark as educational vocabulary for reading hangtags, mill cloth names and generic fiber classes without certifying supply chains, performance claims or animal welfare.
yves-salomon.past: The house is publicly presented as a Paris furrier and outerwear specialist with contemporary ready-to-wear extensions. Atlas inclusion is educational vocabulary for materials literacy, not an endorsement of fur.
